It feels like I'm constantly swinging back and forth between those two extremes.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about the 'wound-up' and 'oddly upbeat' periods, such as how long they lasted and whether you experienced any increased energy, reduced need for sleep, or impulsive behaviors during those times?\n\nPatient: Those wound-up spells have been happening on and off for about a year, usually lasting a few weeks, where I'd have so much energy I couldn't sit still and would wake up before dawn to clean and organize. My thoughts would race so fast that it was almost impossible to shut my brain off to sleep. I even almost threw a large chunk of our savings into an online eco-housing project before my daughter stepped in and talked me down.\n\nDoctor: During those periods when you felt wound-up and oddly upbeat, did you notice any significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or were you still able to manage your daily life and relationships without major issues?\n\nPatient: During those \"up\" periods, I felt like I could handle anything and took on way too many commitments with volunteer projects, even almost making a huge mistake with our savings before my daughter stopped me. However, the severe daily impairment—where I completely stopped working, withdrew from friends, and couldn't do household chores—mostly happens when I sink into those heavy, dark depressions.\n\nDoctor: Did you ever require hospitalization or experience psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, during those wound-up and oddly upbeat periods?\n\nPatient: No, I have never been hospitalized during those wound-up times. I also haven't experienced anything like hearing or seeing things that aren't actually there.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how many days or weeks you typically spend in each of these mood states, and do you usually have a period of normal mood in between the depressed and wound-up phases?\n\nPatient: I'm not quite sure about the exact number of weeks for each phase, or if there is ever a truly normal period in between. Other than that, I haven't noticed any specific day-to-day triggers that suddenly switch me from one state to the other.\n\nDoctor: Can you try to distinguish whether the periods of feeling wound-up are typically followed by a crash into depression, or if they can end without immediately transitioning into a depressive episode?\n\nPatient: Yes, it definitely feels like a direct cycle where those wound-up, high-energy stretches are followed by a crash right back into the dark, heavy depression. I've just been swinging back and forth between those two states over the past year.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the periods of depression and the periods of feeling wound-up have been occurring in a pattern where the depressive episodes are significantly longer, and if so, have you noticed any periods of relatively normal mood in between these episodes over the past year?\n\nPatient: Yes, the heavy depression is definitely much longer and has felt almost constant over the past year, while the wound-up periods are just shorter, intense spells. I sink into these heavy, flat depressions where I feel completely useless and dwell on death, but then a few weeks ago I had a stretch where I felt totally wound-up, wired, and oddly upbeat. It feels like I'm constantly swinging back and forth between those two extremes.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about the 'wound-up' and 'oddly upbeat' periods, such as how long they lasted and whether you experienced any increased energy, reduced need for sleep, or impulsive behaviors during those times?\n\nPatient: Those wound-up spells have been happening on and off for about a year, usually lasting a few weeks, where I'd have so much energy I couldn't sit still and would wake up before dawn to clean and organize.
